root_cause: Queued cancellation persisted a terminal row while its background task kept waiting for one of the two active slots. Repeated submit/cancel freed database admission but accumulated queue tasks. Cancellation of the request after commit could also lose the queue-retirement handoff.
changes: Track jobs only until they acquire a processing slot; remove ownership on task completion even if cancelled before the first coroutine step
After queued cancellation commits, cancel and join its actual queue waiter immediately; a retry of an already cancelled row can retire that same waiter
Keep active and finalizing tasks outside the queue set, preserving existing single-interruption running cancellation and terminal-state semantics
Own and shield cancellation write/result/retirement for an actually queued owner, so a disconnected caller cannot lose the handoff and close still drains it
Expose queued_jobs in service health and handle ordinary and eager task factories without counting active jobs as queued
